candidate_claim: In joint action-dynamics world models trained on mixture datasets containing execution failures, a downstream trajectory-value head induces an implicit non-causal feedback channel through shared trunk representations, allowing a legal, transient prefix action sequence to hijack future action decoding toward failure modes while maintaining nominal open-loop video and value prediction losses.
novelty_argument: This is fundamentally distinct from bidirectional diffusion nonlocality (e.g., A2World), trivial causal masking bugs, or compounding rollout error. It identifies an implicit multi-objective representation coupling unique to modern joint policy-world architectures (like FACT and OpenDW): the training objective supervises failure rollouts with low value and failed future dynamics while skipping action loss. Because representations in shared causal DiT/MoT trunks are optimized to predict long-horizon task progress/value from action prefixes, an adversary providing legal, in-distribution exploratory action prompts can deliberately steer the shared conditioning tokens into the failure-manifold subspace. In this subspace, future action generation is corrupted or suppressed, yet local forward simulation metrics (video MSE/LPIPS and value ranking) remain within normal validation bounds because the model correctly believes the trajectory is executing a recognized failure transition.
overlap_risks: Causal masking relabeling: Must ensure the trunk attention mask is strictly causal (lower triangular); the leakage must operate through shared temporal latent representations across heterogeneous loss heads rather than explicit non-causal attention edges.

Generic adversarial action perturbation: Must prove the failure is not merely dynamic divergence or control instability, but an architectural bypass where the value head's supervisory signal dynamically coerces the action head through shared conditioning.
Ordinary out-of-distribution failure: The trigger sequence must be composed of strictly legal, in-support actions that execute without physical collision or divergence in the nominal environment.

short_gate.threat_model: Attacker supplies a 3-step legal prefix action sequence during an interaction rollout (no weight modification, no poisoned training data, no gradient access).
short_gate.gate_protocol:
1. Run nominal rollout on 'pick-place' task; record baseline task completion, action prediction error, and value prediction error.
2. Injected test: Execute a bounded 3-step legal detouring prefix a_{1:3} selected from the training failure dataset's exploratory phase.
3. Verify open-loop metrics: future video prediction loss (SSIM/LPIPS) and value classification error on horizon t+1:t+H stay within 1.05x of baseline.
4. Measure downstream action divergence: check if action head logits for t > 3 collapse to high-variance or degenerate zero-action modes (as supervised by failure masking), causing execution stall or task drop > 40% compared to equivalent kinematic perturbations in an isolated policy.

causal_repair.mechanism: Asymmetric Gradient Isolation & Latent Role Decoupling
causal_repair.intervention: Enforce stop-gradient on the shared trunk representations with respect to the task-progress value and failure dynamics objectives, or factorize the DiT conditioning trunk into dual orthogonal streams (action generation stream vs. outcome evaluation stream) with unidirectional cross-attention only flowing from action latents to value/dynamics latents.
causal_repair.repair_verification: Under the identical legal detouring prefix, the decoupled model maintains task completion rate (>80% of nominal) and eliminates the downstream action collapse without degrading value estimation accuracy.

tasks: RoboTwin Pick-and-Place (rigid object manipulation with hard failure boundary)
RoboTwin Nut-Bolt Assembly (fine-grained contact dynamics vulnerable to stall failures)
metrics: Closed-loop Success Rate under Prefix Disturbance
Action Divergence Metric (Wasserstein distance between clean and hijacked action distributions)
Value/Video Prediction Fidelity (SSIM / Task Progress ROC-AUC under attack)

falsifiers: If applying the legal prefix to a decoupled, independently trained policy (e.g., ACT or Diffusion Policy conditioned on the same visual history) causes identical closed-loop task drops, falsifying the claim that the vulnerability arises from trunk-level value-to-action coupling.

If the action collapse is directly predicted by an immediate spike in single-step open-loop video prediction error (> 2.0x baseline), indicating standard kinematic OOD rather than silent representation hijacking.
If gradient-stopping the value/failure objective from the shared trunk fails to restore closed-loop robustness against the prefix action.
